subject: WBR prep · Mon 16 Nov 5 pm · Mayank [WBR-20261116-mayank]

questions.text: Mayank, Instamart revenue for 5 Nov – 11 Nov was ₹8,316 against a ₹90,732 target (9.2%), with Tomato Basil 75g - QC accounting for the full −₹82,416 gap, and there was no ad plan for these days (₹805 spend, ROAS 1.22). What happened with this SKU, and was it a stock or listing issue rather than demand?

facts.sku_drivers: Castor Coconut 50ml - QC (−₹37,697); Crushed Tri-Leaf Summer Hair Oil 100 ml - QC (−₹13,005)

questions.text: Dasabuti Hair Oil on Instamart reached ₹1.2 L against a ₹1.9 L target (66.7%, −₹62,096) even though ad spend was ₹38,322 versus a ₹16,683 plan (230%), and discount ran 15.6% against a 7.1% guideline. Why did the extra spend and deeper discount not translate into revenue, particularly on Castor Coconut 50ml - QC (−₹37,697)?

facts.sku_drivers: Fig Rose PrimaLight - QC (−₹31,146); Double Cocoa Intense Dermacare - QC (−₹26,060)

questions.text: Malai Lotion on Instamart delivered ₹59,197 against a ₹1.1 L target (52.0%), while ad spend was ₹83,921 versus a ₹19,250 plan (436%), which puts ad spend at 141.8% of sales and ROAS at 1.01 (down from 2.07). What drove the jump in spend, and what is your view on whether it should continue at this level?

facts.sku_drivers: Neem Beracyl Dandruff Shampoo 250ml - QC (₹10,664); Trileaf Rosemary Shampoo - QC (₹16,573)

questions.text: Shampoo on Instamart beat target at ₹3.9 L versus ₹3.2 L (122.6%), but ad spend was ₹1.5 L against a ₹46,200 plan (318%), or 37.2% of sales versus the platform's 26.4%, with ROAS slipping to 1.62 from 1.71. Was the overspend a deliberate push to capture the upside, and is the return justifying it?

facts.sku_drivers: Tomato Basil Soap 125g - QC (−₹7,288); Lavender 75g - Pack of 3 - QC (−₹2,273)

questions.text: Soap on Instamart came in at ₹3.2 L against a ₹2.9 L target (110.9%), but ad spend was ₹1.1 L versus a ₹48,339 plan (223%), and discount was 12.1% against a 4.7% guideline. Since we were already ahead of target, what was the thinking behind spending and discounting above plan here?

facts.sku_drivers: Tamarind Kasturi - QC (₹22,204); Chandan Nagakesar - QC (₹1.8 L)

questions.text: Lepa on Instamart reached ₹3.2 L against a ₹1.1 L target (277.2%), with Chandan Nagakesar - QC contributing ₹1.8 L, while ad spend was ₹55,774 versus a ₹10,267 plan (543%), though still only 17.5% of sales against the platform's 26.4%. Was the higher spend a deliberate call, and should we be rebasing the plan for Lepa given this run-rate?
